jobs.name: d1
lines: Miss, what's eight percent of fifty? I need a calculator.
No you don't! Just swap the numbers.
Eight percent of fifty is the same as fifty percent of eight.
Fifty percent is half... so it's four?
Yes! Four. It works every time.
Your turn: four percent of seventy-five.

jobs.name: d2
lines: What's ninety-nine times forty-seven? That's impossible in my head.
Think of ninety-nine as a hundred minus one.
Forty-seven times a hundred is four thousand seven hundred.
Exactly! Four thousand six hundred and fifty-three.

jobs.name: d3
lines: Point nine recurring is almost one. But not exactly one, right?
It's exactly one. Watch. Call it x.
Ten x is nine point nine recurring.
So if I take x away... the nines disappear?
Yes! Nine x equals nine. So x equals one.
Point nine recurring is one. Do you believe it? Tell me in the comments.

jobs.name: d4
lines: Ninety-six times ninety-seven. Is there a trick for this?
Yes! How far is each one from a hundred?
Ninety-six take away three is ninety-three. Four times three is twelve.
Put them together. Nine thousand three hundred and twelve!

jobs.name: d5
lines: I can never remember sine thirty or sine sixty.
Use your hand! Your fingers are zero, thirty, forty-five, sixty and ninety degrees.
Fold down the angle's finger. Count the fingers below it. Square root, then divide by two.
Sine thirty: one finger below. Root one over two. A half!
So sine sixty is root three over two?

jobs.name: d6
lines: How many triangles are in this picture? I counted six.
It's easy to miss some. Count the spaces along the bottom.
Now add one plus two plus three plus four.
Ten triangles! Your turn: how many with five spaces?
